status: Concept images for user approval; no gameplay implementation in this iteration
assumption: Mouse near screen edge pans camera
shared_design: Separate non-overlapping cards distributed throughout a larger explorable city
Minimap shows full-city card dots and current viewport

assets.prompt:
Use case: UI concept mockup. Create ONE polished 16:9 landscape gameplay screenshot concept, 1920x1080 feel, for the ancient Three Kingdoms incremental card game 拍案三国. This is a proposed screen for human approval, not an artwork poster. Refined nostalgic Chinese paper print style: warm ivory paper HUD, dark brown ink outlines, cinnabar accents, muted teal, ochre city ground, detailed but quiet woodcut-style top-down art. No photorealism, no 3D, no modern characters, no classroom.
CORE CORRECTION: the city is a large explorable two-dimensional world several times wider and taller than the screen. Many independent portrait paper cards are DISTRIBUTED throughout multiple city neighborhoods. EVERY visible card is fully visible, has its own HP line, upright or only tiny rotation, and has clear empty space around it; no overlapping cards, no central mound, no stacks, no dense grid, no cards obscuring another card. Minimum visual gap between card borders is at least half a card width. Cards rest in open courtyards and street margins, avoid roofs or obstacles. Each is a crisp illustrated general or soldier, dark border, tiny printed star and red health line, similar proportions. Background is overhead / bird's-eye orthographic city: north gate, paved courtyard, tan dirt street, old wooden market awnings, peripheral tiled roofs, southeast waterway and warehouses, southwest tree-lined garden. Terrain extends naturally beyond screenshot edges. Cards must be scattered across the visible play area, not all in center.
HUD: compact parchment top strip roughly 7% of screen height, elegant Chinese title “拍案三国”, location “新野”, coin stat “金币 268”, timer “剩余 24秒”; restrained nav buttons “升级” and “城池”. Compact bottom strip roughly 7% height, four small ancient portraits along lower left with label “上阵”, short hint “单击拍牌 · 滚轮缩放 · 鼠标靠边移动视野”. Do not put a huge empty panel or oversized portrait bar.
MINIMAP IS ESSENTIAL: a clearly readable approximately 230x180 parchment framed minimap in lower RIGHT of playfield above the bottom strip, labeled “新野全图”. It shows the COMPLETE same walled city with north gate, market at northeast, garden at southwest, canal/warehouse at southeast, about 24 scattered cinnabar card dots, and a clean HIGH CONTRAST TEAL RECTANGLE indicating current camera viewport. Rectangle position and size correspond to main camera view. Smaller dots outside rectangle represent offscreen cards. No separate compass image or fake decorative map. This minimap stays same screen size across states.
CURSOR: one small fine cinnabar circular aiming ring with tiny center dot, on the city playfield, no ordinary arrow cursor. No enormous luminous fantasy magic circle. Circle visibly previews single-click slap area. Circle and cards must scale together when camera zoom changes; scale doesn't increase actual range.
No giant explanatory callouts, no flowchart, no panel layout divided into several screenshots, no painted hand covering the playfield. Chinese labels few, clean and readable. Full playable landscape from edge to edge, well organized UI, calm uncluttered ink illustration.
STATE 1: normal gameplay at 100% camera zoom, compact top-right zoom indicator “100%”. Camera viewport covers the NORTHWEST and middle courtyard of the much larger city, north gate and some garden edge visible. Exactly 10 fully separate paper cards, each around 85x120 pixels at 1920x1080, scattered generously in three open areas (left gate courtyard, center street, lower-left garden margin), with broad ground between groups. Keep every card readable and separated; screen is mainly spacious terrain with meaningful exploration. Small aiming circle around 28 pixels radius near center-left card, does not enclose all the cards. Minimap teal viewport rectangle covers about 45% of city width and 45% of city height and sits in the upper-left quadrant; roughly ten red dots inside it correspond to the visible cards, others are outside. This should feel like a useful normal play screen, not an overview of the entire world.
